header.title: Pyramid Texts III: Pepi I: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Pyramid Texts
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:pyramid-texts:pepi:translit, from the UD Egyptian-PC treebank of the Pyramid Texts (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.471.922c: Line 1: ꜥbꜣ may mean 'command' or 'make offering'. Line 3: ꜣwꞽ ('be long, extend') is uncertain here. Line 4: ḥkꜣ.w is 'magic' and also the god Heka.
notes.442.819a: Line 1 plays on nṭꞽ 'thrown down' and Nedit, where Osiris was felled. Line 4: the opening m is read as 'see'.
notes.501C.4: A damaged snake spell. Line 1: sḥsḥ ('run') is uncertain here. Line 2: the verb nꜥ and the noun ꜥr.t ('jaw', or perhaps 'skin') are uncertain. Line 7: šp ('be blind') taken as causative.
notes.477.956a: Line 1: ꜥč̣ is uncertain. Line 3 repeats the opening words of line 4. Line 4: fꜣ.w taken as 'outcry' (also in line 5); nḥm.tꞽ is unclear; ꞽk ('attack') and sꜣḥ ('touch, approach') are uncertain, and pun on the names Iku-ta and Orion (Śꜣḥ). Line 5: čs.n św Śtẖ could also mean 'Seth has raised himself'.
notes.485.1033b: Gehesti (Gḥś.t) is a place name. The 'he' is not named in this line; the line before addresses Geb.
notes.508.1114b: 1114c-1115b: śn ⸗ꞽ is taken as 'my brother'; the clause is uncertain, and śn might instead be a verb ('kiss' or 'pass'). 1115c-1116b: ꜥꜣb.wt is unclear, here taken as jars (or offerings) of water; fṭ.t is read as 'four'.
notes.510.1143b-1144a: Meryre (Mr.y-Rꜥw) is the throne name of Pepi I. 1144b-1145a: ḥbś 'clothe, cover', perhaps of laying the staffs aside; doubtful. 1145c: the Foremost of the Westerners (Ḫnt.ꞽ-ꞽmn.tꞽw) is a god. 1146a: ḥy, here 'flood', is uncertain.

nodes.text: Words to be spoken: So this Great One has fallen on his side; he who is in Nedit has been thrown down.
Your arm is taken by Ra, your head is lifted by the Two Enneads.
Look, he has come as Orion;
see, Osiris has come as Orion, lord of wine at the Wag-festival. 'Beautiful one!' said his mother; 'Heir!' said his father; conceived by the sky, born of the Duat.
The sky has conceived you with Orion; the Duat has borne you with Orion.
It is this Pepi who commands(?) for himself [those] gods [who row] him.
Every god shall rejoice at meeting this Pepi, as they rejoice [at meeting] [Ra] when he comes forth on the eastern side of the sky, in peace, in peace.
Words to be spoken: The sky stretches(?), the earth trembles before this Pepi.
Pepi is Magic;
Pepi is the one who holds magic.
This Pepi has come, that this Pepi may make Orion an *akh* [transfigured spirit], that this Pepi may put Osiris in front, that this Pepi may set the gods on their thrones.
Words to be spoken: The sky is in uproar(?), the earth quakes.
Horus comes, Thoth appears; they raise Osiris from his side and make him stand among the Two Enneads.
Take this word to heart.

Remember, Seth, and take to heart this word which Geb spoke, this outcry(?) which the gods made against you in the Mansion of the Prince in Heliopolis because you threw Osiris to the ground, when you said, Seth, 'I did not do this to him', so that you might have power thereby, being rescued(?), so that you might have power over Horus; when you said, Seth, 'It was he who attacked [me]', [and] this name of his, Earth-Attacker(?), came into being; when you said, Seth, 'It was he who touched(?) me', and this name of his, Orion, came into being, long of leg, wide of stride, foremost of Upper Egypt.
Raise yourself, Osiris! Seth has raised him(?); he has heard the outcry(?) of the gods who spoke about the god's father.
He has found him laid on his side in Gehesti.
Seth runs about(?) because of his testicles.
Horus has spread(?) [his] semen in the jaw(?) of Seth; Seth has spread(?) his semen in the jaw(?) of Horus.
It is a snake.
Lift your face, look at this hand of his!
It is not [his] hand, this;
it is [the claw] of Mafdet, who is [in the midst of] the Mansion.
She will strike you blind(?) in your face,
she will shut you up at your lips,
she will put [...] on your face.
Pepi [goes] to the sky together with the gods who ascend.
'This is my brother(?), this is one who belongs to me,' said Geb. He grasps Pepi by his arm and leads him into the gate of the sky.
The god is in his place.
How good is the god in his place! Satis has purified him with her four *ꜥꜣbt*-jars in Elephantine.
Ah, where then have you come from, my son?
Meryre seizes the sky, its pillars and its stars; the gods come to him bowing.

The *akhs* (transfigured spirits) follow Meryre because of his *ba* (soul); they have covered(?) their staffs, they have broken their weapons for Pepi, for he is a great one, son of a great one, born of Nut.
Pepi's strength is the strength of Seth of Ombos.
This Pepi is the Great Wild Bull who came forth from the Foremost of the Westerners.
Meryre is this efflux of the flood(?); he came forth from it when the water came into being.
